transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well, what brings me in is... I just feel like I’m constantly running on a motor lately. It's like I finish one thing at school, or even just around the house, and I immediately jump right into the next thing. I just never seem to be able to shut myself off.
During this time, have you felt like you need less sleep than usual to feel fully rested?
No, not really. I still need my regular amount of sleep. It's just that when I'm awake, I can't seem to sit still. But my sleep hasn't really changed.
Are you finding yourself constantly worrying or feeling nervous about a lot of different everyday things?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I'm worrying or feeling nervous about things. I mean... I don't have a lot of anxiety about everyday stuff. It's not a nervous energy in my head, it's just... my body just wants to keep going. So no, I don't find myself constantly worrying.
Do you also struggle with paying attention, staying focused on tasks, or being easily distracted?

No, I don't really struggle with that. I can pay attention and stay focused on whatever I need to do. I mean, I'm a special education teacher, so I really have to stay locked in on my students and my work, and I don't have an issue with getting distracted. It's just that... my body can't seem to sit still while I'm doing those things. But my focus itself is fine.
Did you experience these same feelings of restlessness or being constantly on the go when you were a child, before the age of 12?

Yes, I did. My mother actually used to joke that even back in elementary school, I taught the class from my seat. I was just always out of my chair, talking, or... you know, cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So, yes, this has been a part of who I am long before adulthood. It's definitely not something that just started recently with this family change.
